# With AI

## Making it visible

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Agent work goes out from a bot account, a second GitHub login, so
  `git log` tells you who did most of it
- A disclosure line in the Bundibugyo analysis README and on the
  limitations slide of the WHO call about it
- A prompts page with the brief and the steers
- My conference bio was drafted by the bot, "who has a very suspiciously
  high opinion of me, so take it with a pinch of salt"
:::

## Checking what it wrote

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A second agent workflow pulled 114 claims out of one deck and tested
  each against git and the GitHub API
- 67 needed changing
- "530 pull requests" was GitHub's latest issue number. The count was 353
- 712 of 1,371 merged bot pull requests carried no review, so "reviewed by
  me" became "about half"
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-claims.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A single bar of 114 claims, 67 marked changed and 47 marked stood"}

::: {.attribution}
[seabbs/how-I-llm](https://github.com/seabbs/how-I-llm) commits
`8c7e834` and `1fceb9a`, August 2026
:::
:::
::::

## seabbs-review-bot

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A GitHub App. It reviews each pull request I or my bot open, and again
  when either of us asks. A pull request is a proposed change that
  someone reads before it lands
- 213 pull requests reviewed since 17 August 2026. Each review ends "Not
  a human review"
- I fix what it gets right, say which findings I reject and why, and
  check each against the source myself
- It has caught real bugs. It has also been wrong from its own truncated
  greps
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/comms-shot-review-bot.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The GitHub App page for seabbs-review-bot. A robot avatar, the
name, and the line Automated reviews of @seabbs and @seabbs-bot work"}

::: {.attribution}
[github.com/apps/seabbs-review-bot](https://github.com/apps/seabbs-review-bot),
